title: Ercole Rondinelli to Duke of Nevers, 11 November 1590 (Français 3613 — Rondinelli, ff62r–v)

steps.what: George Lasry (with ChatGPT Astra 6 and Anthropic Opus 5.5) transcribed and deciphered the item: 2/2 pages transcribed; Deciphered; 656 elements, 655 identified (99.8%). Report section: Deciphered using a matching key.

Spot-check against the Gallica image (https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b90582263/f69.item): f62r "Ser.mo Principe Sig.re et Pron mio Col.mo", full cipher in letter-substitution with superscript vowels; his key image is the original "Cifra col S. Cav. Giac. Gratij" (Fr. 3995 f89: a=8, b=7, c=6, d=5, f=m, n=h, r=y, s=theta, t=g...), alphabet consistent with the cipher letters; superscript (babuino) syllables made a quick run-decode inconclusive Verdict: partly confirmed.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked George Lasry's report excerpt (lasry_entry.md); his full transcription and decryption are not in the repository

texts.summary: Ercole Rondinelli to the Duke of Nevers, 11 November 1590. Rondinelli describes Catholic dissatisfaction, preparations against Paris, and doubts about the Duke of Mena protecting the city.
texts.note: The repository holds only the excerpt and translation in George Lasry's report (lasry_entry.md); his full transcription and decryption are his and not yet in the repository, and the ciphertext has not been transcribed here.

reading_review.note: Rests on George Lasry's report excerpt (f. 62r, cipher lines 15-17; lasry_excerpt_reading.md), one complete coherent Italian sentence with no holes (Mayenne is not able to defend it, being governed by those who want his ruin). His report says 2/2 pages transcribed, deciphered; the repository text is only this fragment, his full decryption is not here.
